shared_elements: incised linear grooves cut into a rounded stone surface
curved arc-shaped lines suggestive of eye/brow or mouth features
possible schematic face motif on a boulder-like form
justification: Both show shallow incised curvilinear grooves worked into the convex surface of a rounded stone mass, and in each case the lines can be read as schematic facial features (arcs for brow/eye and mouth), which is the most specific correspondence. However, A presents a compact, deliberately shaped head with paired bosses for eyes and a dense field of regular crosshatched/grid lattice lines over its lower half, whereas B's carving is a sparse set of isolated arcs on a natural outcrop with no comparable lattice infill or defined head outline, so the shared content stays at the generic level of "incised lines that may make a face."
